mission.title: High Life
mission.description: Help Flood show the intruder everything the Merovingian's organization has to offer.

npc.say: This is not what I came here for.
There is nothing of a young man's blood in this one's body or mind.
Christeen! Throw this out! Yes, all of it! It's trash! Bah! Bring the melanzane! We'll whip something up!
He's tough, but I'm learning a lot.
I'll take no more stuffing from this program.
I can work with this guy.
That bubble skin of his is interesting... I'll have to ask him about that.
I wouldn't want him hanging around, anyway.
He'll know when I want him to know.

phase.briefing: The intruder as yet fails to grasp the full extent of our allure. It's time to give him the full-court press...well, at least with those who I don't particularly mind putting in harm's way. Yes, that means you're going along too, {player}. Just try to make sure everything goes as smoothly as my immaculate plan deserves.

enter.say:
Yep, as usual, we'll get blamed if anything goes wrong. Good thing nobody actually takes Flood as seriously as he likes to think they do.
Looks like he isn't messing around, though, 'cause he's starting out with the big gun: Persephone. Better make sure the boss' wife is all right.

talk.say:
Hmh. This simulation is a far cry from--
No, never mind. You'll excuse me if I outgrew the charms of beauty long ago.

done.say: Probably what happens when you turn into wireframes. See what Persephone thinks of him.

talk.say: I expected as much from an acquaintance of Flood. He does not know himself.

done.say: Ouch. Might want to keep that first part out of our report...

phase.briefing:
Phaugh... Persephone has become sullen and pale--a liability, if you ask me. Fortunately, we have other agents who can demonstrate to him the benefits of our organiza-- Hold on.
What? The hell you say! Move those cakes! Yes, yes; I'll take care of the rest.
Lovely. The Machines are trying to horn in. Please deal with them for me; then we can get on with business.

enter.say:
Cakes?
Whatever. Probably best we didn't find out.
All right, hostile programs are all over that place. No cake for them.

objective.text: Kill all of the hostile programs

done.say: That takes care of that. We'd better catch up with Flood.

phase.briefing: Hm! Well...good job. Now hurry up, we're running late!

enter.say:
Ya know, if this guy would just tell us what he's after, it would make all this a whole lot easier.
Looks like it's the Chef's turn to butter our linear buddy up.
But...does he even eat?

talk.say:
Eh? It's all a matter of sensory inputs, my boy. Don't tell me that you don't have the right receptors? Not that it matters; we could--
Oh, you do? Then tell me the scent of that fresh Pansette de Gerzat doesn't get your taste buds tingling!

done.say:
Maybe Flood should have picked someone a little less over the top.
He isn't actually eating that stuff, is he?

talk.say: It's almost amusing that they saved all these...trappings of a dead culture--things they were never designed to enjoy. They'd better not be losing their sense of perspective.

done.say: Jeez, I can't tell if this is making an impression or not. Flood better come up with something good...

phase.briefing: No appreciation for cuisine, hm? There's got to be something he'll bite on. Don't stand too close to him, {player}. You're probably putting him off his feed.

enter.say: Ooh, a triple threat this time. I guess it's now or never.

talk.say:
Sure, you got the glitter thing going on there, man, but you've got to focus it, you know what I mean? Right now you're just one big bright spot. What you want to do is draw the eye to your best sides. Strategy.
Now, what I'm seeing for you... Hold it... Yeah, yeah. Okay, imagine this: a solid gold circlet, right above the brow there. It would give you weight, man; you're just kind of...whoosh! --floating off, you know? And it would solve the eyebrow problem. I'm telling you, it'd be perfect. Just think how the gold would catch the light from those lines of yours.
If I've ever seen anyone who needed some work... But he said he didn't want any alteration.
I gave him one of my most reliable numbers; not much reaction. He isn't relaxed--won't let the music move him. It's wasted on someone like that.

done.say: Dang, it doesn't sound like we made a dent.

talk.say:
I have no use for digital substitutes; it's reality I'm after.
But if your master has access to all of these...it could be that he'd be of use.

done.say: Hey, whoa, maybe that did work--a little. Still isn't much for giving clues though, is he?

mission.finish:
That's because I'm able to outthink these people, operative. I can tell what he's after.
No, I'm not going to tell you. You wouldn't appreciate it. Just keep following my lead, and soon he'll be eating out of our hand--figuratively speaking.
